# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue, indicated by the doctor, but the specifics were not fully understood by the parent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties, including getting upset during feeds and having trouble latching on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a brain issue, specifically a tethered cord, which causes pain, weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause similar issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty with his ears, covering his ears when exposed to loud noise, and getting frustrated when it's too loud.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have hearing problems, including recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems, including astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia), and squint (strabismus).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth that are also sensitive, and the parent is taking good care of them to prevent further issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and the potential for tooth decay.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had challenges with feeding, but these seem to have sorted themselves out now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some children with KBG syndrome have had challenges with feeding, requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient stands and walks differently, and there is something with his hips, possibly dysplasia, which is hard to keep track of.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of people with KBG syndrome have a brain issue, specifically a tethered cord, which can cause similar issues.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of people with KBG syndrome have a tethered cord, which can cause similar issues.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screen for hearing issues: Regular hearing reviews to age 5, even if earlier reviews give a clear response.
b) Screen for vision issues: Check position of testes in boys, consider a palate review, and refer for a cardiac review following diagnosis.
c) Screen for feeding issues: Feeding was tricky when the patient was little, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.
d) Screen for heart valve issues: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.
e) Screen for tethered cord: One study found that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause similar issues.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent monitoring of the heart due to potential congenital heart defects, with echocardiograms and ECGs being conducted regularly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve abnormalities, chamber holes, and structural changes, requiring monitoring and potential surgical intervention.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is extremely picky about food textures, refusing to eat anything except what they perceive as safe, leading to mealtime stress and difficulty in finding suitable foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome exhibit selective eating habits, preferring familiar textures and avoiding unfamiliar ones, potentially leading to nutritional deficiencies and digestive issues.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits hypotonia, with weakened muscles affecting movement and balance, necessitating physical therapy to strengthen muscles.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, contributing to reduced muscle strength and coordination.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, particularly with texture, and may require short-term nasogastric tube feeding supplements.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, especially with texture, and may require specialized dietary interventions or supplementation.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems, including astigmatism, short-sightedness, and squinting, which can impact reading and social interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision issues are common in KBG syndrome, including refractive errors and ocular deformities, which can lead to visual impairments and challenges in daily activities.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are prone to chipping and breaking, requiring frequent dental visits to address various dental issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth issues are a common feature in KBG syndrome, with high rates of tooth sensitivity and susceptibility to decay.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with communication and understanding, making it challenging for peers and educators to interact effectively.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Communication difficulties are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, impacting academic performance and social interaction.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety, requiring additional support and accommodations in educational settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences are common in KBG syndrome, contributing to social and emotional challenges that may require tailored support and accommodations.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, resulting in an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and may experience hip dysplasia, leading to potential mobility issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies are a characteristic feature of KBG syndrome, with variations in bone structure and potential musculoskeletal complications.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screen for hearing and vision issues early in life to prevent future complications.
b) Monitor heart health closely throughout the patient's lifetime to detect and address potential congenital heart defects.
c) Implement a comprehensive feeding program to accommodate the patient's picky eating habits and ensure adequate nutrition.
d) Address speech and communication needs through targeted therapies and accommodations in educational settings.
e) Manage orthopedic issues, such as brachydactylia and clinodactyly, through physical therapy and corrective measures.
f) Evaluate and manage dental issues, including tooth sensitivity and chipping, through regular dental care and possible restorative procedures.
g) Conduct regular cardiovascular assessments to monitor for potential heart conditions and provide timely interventions.
h) Perform periodic ophthalmological evaluations to address vision issues and correct refractive errors.
i) Monitor growth patterns and adjust dietary intake accordingly to prevent stunted growth or malnutrition.
j) Identify and address behavioral differences through therapeutic interventions and accommodations in educational settings.
k) Develop personalized treatment plans for orthopedic and neurodevelopmental issues, incorporating physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as necessary.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hearing difficulties, particularly with certain sounds, and has a feeding aversion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, indicating variability in auditory and digestive systems.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, affecting her vision, and requires corrective lenses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have hearing difficulties, suggesting variability in visual and auditory systems.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups due to a condition that was identified early on, and the doctors keep a close eye on it to ensure everything stays under control.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky with food textures and some foods he won't eat because of how they feel in his mouth. They are trying to gradually introduce new textures to help him get used to variety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone. It is being managed with physiotherapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting muscle tone.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which is being managed with physical therapy and regular exercises to strengthen his back muscles.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Scoliosis is a common feature in KBG syndrome, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences blurred vision, requiring regular eye checks to address potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia) are common in KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel and is taking good care of their teeth with regular brushing and dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is a common concern in KBG syndrome, emphasizing the importance of proper tooth care.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient attends a nursery and requires additional help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and it is being managed with physiotherapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting muscle tone.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which is being managed with physical therapy and regular exercises to strengthen his back muscles.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Scoliosis is a common feature in KBG syndrome, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screen for heart conditions: Regular heart check-ups are recommended due to the presence of a condition that was identified early on.
b) Address vision issues: Regular eye checks are recommended to address potential hearing issues.
c) Manage scoliosis: Physical therapy and regular exercises are recommended to strengthen the back muscles.
d) Monitor growth: Monitoring growth velocity is recommended, especially if the patient's height is below the 2nd centile.
